MEDICALS EXAMINATION CAN MAKE OR BREAK YOUR NDA/CDS JOURNEY — KNOW THE PROCESS BEFORE YOU REACH SSB.  Clearing the written exam and SSB is a major milestone, but medical fitness is another important stage of the selection process.  In this 5-part series, understand what happens during the NDA/CDS medical examination:  General Physical Examination  Height, weight, BMI/proportion, spine, joints, chest, abdomen, skin, hernia, varicose veins, previous injuries and other physical conditions.  Eyes, ENT & Dental  Visual acuity, colour perception, field of vision, eye examination, hearing, ears, nose, throat, sinuses, speech and dental assessment.  Investigations & Special Tests  Depending on the entry and medical requirements, candidates may undergo blood and urine tests, X-ray, USG abdomen, ECG and specialist examinations.  Medical History Matters  Relevant previous illness, surgery, injury or treatment should be disclosed truthfully during the medical process.  Fit, Unfit & Appeal/Review  The Medical Board determines medical status according to the applicable Armed Forces standards and procedures. Standards can vary by entry and branch, with additional requirements for flying/aircrew roles.  Important: Medical standards are different from ordinary civilian health standards and can change with official policy. Always refer to the latest official notification and medical standards applicable to your entry.  Aspirant tip: Don't wait until SSB to think about medical fitness. If you have a persistent health concern, get it evaluated by a qualified doctor well in advance. SSB SCREENING IS NOT ABOUT BEING THE LOUDEST — IT’S ABOUT BEING CLEAR, LOGICAL AND NATURAL.  Clearing Stage 1 starts with understanding the basics:  OIR: Focus on speed + accuracy. Practice verbal reasoning, non-verbal reasoning, analogy, classification, series, coding-decoding and basic mathematical reasoning.  PPDT: Observe the picture carefully, understand the situation, identify the central problem and build a logical, realistic, action-oriented story.  Remember the simple structure: Situation → Action → Result  Group Discussion: Quality matters more than quantity. Speak clearly, give relevant points, listen to others, build on good ideas, stay calm and give everyone a chance to contribute.  Avoid common mistakes: • Memorising or copying stories • Making stories unrealistic • Speaking just to speak • Dominating the discussion • Losing confidence after disagreement • Ignoring other candidates’ points  The goal is simple: OBSERVE WELL. THINK LOGICALLY. SPEAK CONFIDENTLY. STAY NATURAL. What happens if India’s Vice President resigns? 🇮🇳  The Vice President of India, who is also the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, can resign by giving a letter to the President. Once accepted, the office falls vacant immediately.  The complete process:  Vacancy Notification: The Election Commission is informed.  Constitutional Rule: As per Article 68(1), a new Vice President must be elected as soon as possible.  Who Votes? Only members of both Houses of Parliament vote (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha).  Election Method: Proportional representation through a single transferable vote (STV) by secret ballot.  Acting VP: Until then, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha handles the Vice President’s duties.  The new Vice President serves a full 5-year term, not just the remainder of the previous term. 🏛️ How a Bill Becomes a Law in India – Step-by-Step Explanation  1️⃣ Drafting  A Bill is first drafted. It can be proposed by a Minister (Government Bill) or any MP (Private Member's Bill). It is introduced in either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.  2️⃣ First Reading  The title and main objectives of the Bill are read out. 👉 No detailed discussion or voting happens at this stage.  3️⃣ Second Reading  This is the most important stage: ✔️ Full debate on the Bill ✔️ May be sent to a Parliamentary Committee ✔️ Amendments can be proposed and discussed  4️⃣ Third Reading  A final discussion is held, mainly on whether to pass the Bill as a whole. 🗳 Members vote on it. If passed → it moves to the other House.  5️⃣ Second House  The same 3 readings (1st, 2nd, and 3rd) take place in the second House. ✅ If passed in both Houses, the Bill moves to the President.  6️⃣ President’s Assent  The President either: ✔️ Approves (Signs) → It becomes a Law (Act) ❌ Or sends it back (only for non-money bills) 📌 If sent again and passed → President must give assent.  📌 From Drafting to President’s Assent – this is the full journey of a Bill in Parliament.  💯 Perfect for NDA, UPSC, SSC & other competitive exams!  👉 Save it. 📚 Sources of the Indian Constitution –  India didn’t just write a Constitution—it curated the BEST ideas from across the world 🌍 Here’s a breakdown of key features and where they were borrowed from 👇  ✅ Fundamental Rights – USA 🇺🇸 Inspired by the Bill of Rights in the U.S. Constitution, India adopted similar basic rights such as freedom of speech, equality, and protection of life and liberty.  ✅ Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) – Ireland 🇮🇪 India adopted the idea of DPSPs from the Irish Constitution to promote social and economic justice. These are not enforceable but guide governance.  ✅ Parliamentary System – UK 🇬🇧 India’s system of government (Prime Minister + Council of Ministers) is based on the British parliamentary model—with a nominal head (President) and a real head (PM).  ✅ Federal System with Strong Centre – Canada 🇨🇦 Like Canada, India is a quasi-federal state, meaning it has a federal structure but a strong central government that holds more power during crises.  ✅ Procedure Established by Law – Japan 🇯🇵 Unlike the U.S. "due process of law," India adopted "procedure established by law" from Japan, meaning that laws must be followed as passed by the legislature, even if unjust—though later evolved by Indian judiciary.  ✅ Concurrent List – Australia 🇦🇺 India borrowed the idea of a Concurrent List from the Australian Constitution, allowing both Centre and States to make laws on certain topics like education, forests, marriage, etc.  ✅ Emergency Provisions – Germany 🇩🇪 Inspired by the Weimar Constitution of Germany, India included strong emergency powers—National, State, and Financial—empowering the President to act decisively.  ✅ Independent Judiciary – USA 🇺🇸 Like the USA, India adopted the concept of an independent judiciary to protect the Constitution and citizens’ rights. The Supreme Court acts as the guardian of justice.  ✅ Justice, Liberty, Equality – France 🇫🇷 The Preamble of our Constitution reflects ideals of the French Revolution: Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity—forming the foundation of a secular democratic republic.  📌 Save this post for quick revision!  #ndawallah #indianpolity #polity

Chandrayaan-3 is India's third lunar mission, launched on 14 July 2023. It successfully soft-landed on the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land a spacecraft in this region.  The mission's objectives are to:  Demonstrate a safe and soft landing on the lunar surface  Demonstrate rover roving on the Moon  Conduct in-situ scientific experiments  The spacecraft consists of a lander, a rover, and a propulsion module. The lander, Vikram, is named after the Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-2, which was lost during the final descent to the Moon. The rover, Pragyan, is named after the Sanskrit word for "wisdom." The propulsion module, Chandrayaan-3 Orbiter, will remain in orbit around the Moon to provide communications and navigation support for the lander and rover.  The lander and rover are carrying a number of scientific instruments to study the Moon's surface and atmosphere. The lander will conduct experiments to measure the lunar surface's composition and structure. The rover will explore the lunar surface and collect samples for analysis.  Chandrayaan-3 is a major achievement for India's space program. It demonstrates India's technological prowess and its commitment to space exploration.  Here are some of the key milestones of the Chandrayaan-3 mission:  14 July 2023: Chandrayaan-3 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, India.  23 August 2023: Vikram lander successfully soft-landed on the Moon's south pole.  24 August 2023: Pragyan rover successfully deployed from Vikram lander.  Chandrayaan-3 is still in its early stages, but it has already made history. India is now a leading player in space exploration, and Chandrayaan-3 is sure to inspire future generations of scientists and engineers.  #ndawallah #physicswallah #currentaffairs #August2023 #ndapreparation #alakhpandey #chandrayan3 #softlaunch #Chandrayaan3Landing #SouthPole

PHYSICAL QUANTITIES   The quantities which can be measured directly or indirectly and by means of which we can describe the laws of physics are called physical quantities . e.g. length , mass , volume etc.   Physical quantities are of two types   ( i ) Fundamental Quantities The quantities which do not depend upon other quantities for their complete definition are known as fundamental or base quantities .   There are seven fundamental quantities Length , Mass , Time , Electric current , Thermodynamic temperature , Luminous intensity , Amount of substance .   ( ii ) Derived Quantities The quantities which can be expressed in terms of the fundamental quantities are called derived quantities . e.g. , speed , volume , acceleration , force , etc   Note :-   Other than fundamental and derived quantities there are two more quantities called as supplementary quantities . e.g. , plane angle and solid angle .
